newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: REINZ says still room for lower NZ mortgage rates.
newsitem.headline: REINZ says still room for lower NZ mortgage rates.

text.p: The Real Estate Institute of New Zealand said on Friday that recent mortgage rate cuts would boost confidence in the residential property market and there was room for further falls.

"There is still room for competition among lenders to take interest rates even lower and we could even see a further drop in the second half of the year," REINZ President Colin Brown said in a statement.
Brown did not expect a dramatic rise in house prices or a property boom. Most REINZ members across the country were reporting "fairly healthy" sales figures over the past few months.
Fixed rates were proving a very affordable option but buyers were increasingly being attracted to the range of floating rates on offer, he said.
The first REINZ mortage rate survey for the year showed all but two lending institutions had cut floating rates from the previous month, while most had also lowered fixed rates.
Floating rates now range from 9.5 percent to 10.5 percent. Fixed rates range from 8.75 percent to 9.95 percent for one year and 8.65 to 9.25 percent over three years.
